captions.detailed: This 3D model is a multi-part kit designed for an electronic ice fishing tip-up alert system, presented here arranged flat on a build plate. It features two symmetrical halves of a rectangular enclosure, each containing custom-molded internal cavities, cylindrical channels, and support structures to secure a buzzer, tilt switch, LED, resistor, and an A23 battery. Also included in the layout are two rectangular retainer clips to clamp the housing halves together, and a separate flat mounting flange with a rod-attachment guide. The parts are designed with precise tolerances to fit together snugly after printing.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric, multi-part OpenSCAD script for an ice fishing 'Fish-On' alarm enclosure. The script should generate a split rectangular case (left and right halves) with internal compartments tailored to a buzzer, LED, tilt switch, slide switch, and A23 battery, while including adjustable parameters for the rod attachment diameter, retainer clip fit tolerance, and cable tie dimensions.
captions.factory: The script uses a modular structure to define individual parts: 'leftHolder', 'rightHolder', 'rodAttachment', and 'retainerClip'. The main enclosure halves are created by taking a solid base block ('holder') and using 'difference' to subtract cylindrical, spherical, and cubic primitives corresponding to the electronic components (buzzer, battery, LED, switches) and wiring channels. Slicing the main holder into left and right halves is achieved using 'difference' with a large boundary cube. The parts are arranged for printing on a build plate using conditional 'if' statements based on the 'part' parameter, utilizing 'translate' and 'rotate' operations.
